payload.title: Decide reachability reporting for gold with no detector concept
payload.description:
There are 15 rules in `patterns/pii-signals.rules.yaml`. Against them, **422 of 793** mention and data-item gold cases match no rule under any alias:

- unreachable mention concepts: `access_token` x39, `credential_secret` x29, `password_verifier` x13, `payment_card_data` x6, `employment_information` x5, `city` x5, `compensation` x4
- unreachable data items: 308 of 436 are **source field names**, not concepts — `id` x17, `name` x8, `token` x7, `location` x5, `city` x5, `status` x3, `key` x3, `uid` x3, `uuid` x3

Ceilings with today's rule set, perfect matching assumed: **~68% mention recall, ~29% data-item recall.**

These cases are eligible — the file was read successfully — and permanently missed, because no detector concept exists. No eligibility reason describes that state, and a closed one-to-one leaf map cannot create leaves that do not exist.

**Proposed decision.** Report a `reachable` denominator beside `evaluablePositives` as a diagnostic. This does **not** exclude anything: KDATAP-08a0ac rightly rejects removing known gaps from raw metrics, and raw recall still counts every miss. It is a second denominator so a reader can separate three different zeros — a detector missed it, no concept exists for it, or gold and engine name it differently.

Without it, the first published data-item figure reads as detector quality when it is dominated by gold keyed on raw source field names.

Rejected: excluding unreachable cases from recall; a `documentedGap`-style suppression flag; publishing a single recall number with no coverage context.
